title: A French Crowd Just Lost It Over a Telugu Film: Rajamouli's 'Varanasi' Storms Annecy
excerpt: The first glimpse, 'Varanasi: To the World', drew cheers and a standing ovation at the world's most prestigious animation festival — and Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra and Prithviraj haven't even shot the whole thing yet.
body:
The lights went down in a French alpine town better known for hand-drawn fairy tales, and what flickered onto the screen was a charging bull, a futuristic war machine, and a city older than memory. By the time **Varanasi: To the World** had finished playing at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival this week, the room was on its feet. People cheered. People applauded. Somewhere in the back, a few thousand kilometres from the ghats it's named after, a Telugu film about an Indian holy city had just conquered a French crowd that didn't need subtitles to feel the scale of it.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=eHRcfjJZaRM</youtube>

This is the thing about **S.S. Rajamouli**: he doesn't release footage, he detonates it. After *Baahubali* and *RRR* turned him into the most globally bankable storyteller India has ever produced, the man could have coasted. Instead he's spent nearly three years and a reported ₹1,300 crore building **Varanasi** — an action-adventure that, by every account leaking out of the edit bay, is bigger than anything he's attempted. Annecy, the most prestigious animation showcase on the planet, was simply the latest stage he chose to set on fire.

> The theatre was filled with excitement as people cheered and applauded throughout the presentation. While the film is yet to arrive in cinemas, it is already making waves across the globe.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DaCdjZCpLAl/

Let's talk about who's in it, because the casting alone makes this a must-watch. **Mahesh Babu** — Tollywood royalty, a star who has spent two decades being the most effortlessly cool man in any frame — is making his first-ever collaboration with Rajamouli. That sentence should make any South cinema fan sit up. Opposite him is **Priyanka Chopra Jonas**, returning to Indian cinema not for a favour or a cameo but for a lead role in the most expensive film of her career, a homecoming the diaspora has been waiting years to see. And **Prithviraj Sukumaran**, Malayalam cinema's most magnetic intensity, rounds out a trio that spans three industries and one enormous ambition. Rajamouli has reportedly praised Priyanka's "ferocity and vulnerability," and if you've seen what he did with Alia Bhatt's single scene in *RRR*, you know he doesn't hand out adjectives lightly.

The glimpse itself trades in beautiful contradictions. Charging bulls in dust-caked traditional settings cut against gleaming, high-concept machinery. Ancient and futuristic, sacred and synthetic, all colliding in the same frame. Nobody outside the production knows exactly what *Varanasi* is about — the plot is a vault Rajamouli guards like scripture — but the whispers are intoxicating: a globe-trotting story unfolding across multiple timelines, with a shoot that has reportedly chased its cast all the way to Antarctica. If that holds, Rajamouli would become the first Indian filmmaker to capture a major commercial production on the frozen continent, joining a list of films so short you could count them on one hand.

Backing the spectacle is the same powerhouse machine that built the legend: veteran writer **V. Vijayendra Prasad** on script, Academy Award winner **M.M. Keeravani** on the score. The budget, north of ₹1,300 crore before print and publicity, makes *Varanasi* one of the two costliest films India has ever mounted — second only to the upcoming *Ramayana*. And yet, in a flex that's almost arrogant, Rajamouli has said he intends to keep the runtime under three hours. Shorter than *RRR*. For a film this enormous, that's not restraint. That's a director showing off.

For the diaspora, the global rollout has been the tell. *Varanasi* made its first international appearance not in Hyderabad but in Mexico City, at CCXP, before landing at Annecy in France. Rajamouli isn't building this for the front-bench crowd alone; he's building it for the NRI in New Jersey, the student in Manchester, the family in Toronto who turned *RRR* into a midnight phenomenon and screamed "Naatu Naatu" until it won an Oscar. When *Varanasi* hits theatres on **April 7, 2027**, expect the same diaspora multiplexes that sold out *Baahubali 2* to do it all over again — likely in Telugu, Tamil, Hindi, and English, across the US, UK, and Canada.

That's still nine months away. Nine months of teases, glimpses, and engineered hysteria, each one designed to make the wait feel unbearable. On the evidence of one French festival crowd losing its composure over three minutes of footage, it's working. Rajamouli hasn't shown us the film yet. He's just shown us that, once again, the whole world is going to come watch.
